blocks.text: **Software** is the set of programs, instructions and related information that tells a computer what to do. Hardware is the machine you can touch; software is what makes it useful.

blocks.title: Key terms
rows: Programs, instructions and associated information used to perform computer tasks
An organised set of instructions that the computer follows
Software made for smartphones and tablets
A functional component that does one particular job; several cooperating modules can form an application

blocks.title: Module is not the smallest unit
blocks.text: A **module** is a component that performs a job, but it is not universally the smallest software unit. Do not choose it as the answer to 'smallest unit of software'.

blocks.title: Stages and terms
rows: The original instructions written by a programmer
Output of a compiler or assembler; native object files hold machine instructions plus linking information
Instructions a processor can run directly, represented in binary
Combines object files and the libraries they need into linked output
A file prepared to run as a program
Places a program in memory and prepares it to run

blocks.title: From source code to a running program
items: Ready to run, e.g. .exe on Windows

blocks.text: **.exe** means executable and is a common Windows executable extension. Not all software uses .exe.

blocks.title: Program vs process vs package
rows: An executing instance of a program, with its own state and resources
Software distributed as one unit: program files, supporting resources and documentation
A traditional group of small supporting apps such as Calculator, a text editor and Paint

blocks.text: In the Accessories group, **Paint** is a drawing app, while **Word** is a word processor. Do not mix them up.

blocks.title: People who work with software
rows: Designs and builds software; the roles overlap
Widely recognised as the first computer programmer, for her work on Babbage's Analytical Engine

blocks.title: Quick memory line
blocks.text: Source = original code | Process = running program | .exe = Windows executable.
Software has two main groups. **System software** manages the hardware and system resources and supports other programs. **Application software** helps users perform specific tasks.

blocks.title: Where software sits
items: Word, Excel, browser, Tally, media player
Talk to and control the hardware

blocks.title: System software components
rows: Manages processes, memory, files and devices and provides services to applications
Gives the OS an interface to talk to hardware, e.g. printer, graphics, audio and network drivers
Maintain, protect and manage the system and its data
Software closely tied to a device's basic operation

blocks.text: **MS-DOS** is an operating system, so it is system software, not application software. Communication software needs context: apps are applications, OS networking parts are system software.

blocks.title: Common utility tools
rows: Removes selected temporary and unnecessary files
Copies data so it can be recovered later
Reduces the storage space needed by suitable data

blocks.text: Utilities support reliability, security and efficiency. Some improve performance, but not every utility makes the computer faster.

blocks.title: Fragmentation and defragmentation
rows: A file's data ends up stored in separate, scattered locations
Reorganises the scattered file fragments on a hard disk so they can be read more efficiently

blocks.title: Cleanup is not defragmentation
blocks.text: **Disk Cleanup** deletes unnecessary data; **defragmentation** rearranges existing data. Defragmentation is not just collecting folders or separating used and unused space.
Windows optimises HDDs and SSDs differently. For SSDs the optimisation commonly uses **TRIM**.

Application software is also called **end-user software**. **General-purpose** applications serve common needs, while **special-purpose** applications handle a defined job such as payroll or ticket reservation.

blocks.title: Common applications
rows: Play audio and video, e.g. VLC Media Player, Windows Media Player
Built or adapted for a customer's requirements

blocks.title: Enterprise software
rows: Enterprise Resource Planning: integrates business activities such as finance, purchasing, inventory and human resources
A company that supplies business software, including ERP applications

blocks.text: **ERP** is a software category; **SAP** is a company that supplies business software (including ERP). They are not the same thing.

blocks.title: Horizontal vs vertical software
rows: Word processors, spreadsheets, general collaboration tools
Banking platforms, hospital-management and hotel-management systems
Developed or adapted for one organisation
A system built to one bank's own needs

blocks.text: Vertical software can be a standard product or a custom solution, so the two terms are not identical. **On-demand** describes how software is delivered, not an automatic synonym for vertical software.

blocks.title: Banking examples
rows: Banking software developed by Infosys; a vertical software example
A UK payment system supporting Direct Debit and Direct Credit; not the name of a core banking software package

blocks.text: Horizontal = many industries, like a wide road. Vertical = one industry, like a tall tower. Application = user task, ERP = integrated business processes.

blocks.title: Open source
rows: The licence makes source code available and permits use, modification and redistribution under stated conditions
Can be supplied free or sold commercially
Linux kernel, Mozilla Firefox, Apache OpenOffice, VLC Media Player
Android Open Source Project; Android devices may also contain proprietary apps and components

blocks.text: Open source does not simply mean free of charge or easy to edit. Programming skill may still be needed to modify it.

blocks.title: Closed source
rows: Source code is usually withheld and modification is restricted by the owner
Microsoft Office, Tally, many SAP applications, Avast Antivirus

blocks.text: A free edition of Avast is not automatically open source. Free to use and open source are different ideas.

blocks.title: Distribution terms
rows: Supplied without a purchase price, subject to licence terms; source code need not be available
Distributed for evaluation; payment is expected or required for continued use or extra features
Evaluation software limited by time, features or usage; commonly a form of shareware
Shows repeated pop-up reminders to register, buy or pay

blocks.title: Things to note
items: **VLC** is free of charge AND open source.
Older material lists **Internet Explorer** as a browser supplied without a separate purchase price.
Antivirus products such as **Kaspersky** and **Quick Heal** may have trial or paid editions. Antivirus is a function, not a licence type.
Redistribution of shareware depends on its licence; it is not automatically allowed for everyone.

blocks.title: EULA, public domain and piracy
rows: End User License Agreement: terms for an end user's use of software, such as installation, copying, permitted devices and restrictions
Unauthorised copying, distribution or use that violates rights or licence terms

blocks.text: **Freeware** and **open-source** software can still be copyrighted. Being freely available does not make software public domain.

blocks.title: Languages
rows: High-Level Language, with abstractions easier to use than machine instructions, e.g. Python, Java, C++
A low-level language; the assembler is its translator, not a programming language

blocks.text: Programmers commonly use high-level languages but can also write assembly or other low-level code.

blocks.title: Translators compared
rows: Translates source code into another form (assembly, object code, machine code or bytecode) before it is executed
May work in several passes and compile separate files
Executes a program through a runtime, commonly processing statements or intermediate instructions progressively
'Line by line' is a simplified exam description
Converts assembly-language instructions into machine-code object output
High-level to assembly is a compiler task

blocks.title: Assembler correction
blocks.text: Converting a high-level language into assembly language is a **compiler** task, not an assembler task. Also, not every compiler emits native machine code directly.

blocks.title: A typical native build
items: Loader prepares the program to run

blocks.title: Java and debugger
rows: Java Virtual Machine: runs bytecode using interpretation and, in many implementations, just-in-time compilation
Helps inspect execution and locate defects; a separate tool, not a language translator

blocks.text: Java is the common exam example of **compilation plus interpretation**.
**Malware** means malicious software, created to steal data, damage systems, disrupt operations or gain unauthorised access.

blocks.title: Kinds of malware
rows: Infects host files or programs and spreads when the infected code runs
Self-replicates and can spread without attaching to a host file
Looks legitimate while doing harmful things
Hides malicious activity or helps keep privileged access
Locks systems or encrypts data and demands payment
Unwanted advertising with harmful or intrusive behaviour

blocks.text: Advertising-supported software is not automatically malware. Only adware with harmful or intrusive behaviour counts.

blocks.title: Maintenance terms
rows: A software defect causing incorrect or unexpected behaviour
Identifying and resolving system, app or device problems
A targeted fix for defects, vulnerabilities or behaviour
Fixes, security improvements or smaller feature changes
A move to a newer or more capable version, usually with larger changes

blocks.text: Patches need not be online or free. Upgrading does not require you to manually uninstall the old version first.

blocks.title: Firmware
rows: Software stored in non-volatile memory to control a device's basic functions
BIOS/UEFI, remote controls, printers, routers, traffic-signal controllers and other embedded devices
ROM is the traditional exam answer; EEPROM and rewritable flash are also used

blocks.text: Firmware is software associated with hardware. It is not literally 'hardware plus software' and it does not replace hardware.

blocks.title: Middleware
rows: Shared software services that connect applications, components, clients, servers and data sources
The 'glue' between components; it can provide services between applications and the operating system
Supplies shared services inside embedded systems, including those using a real-time OS

blocks.text: Bug = defect | Patch = targeted fix | Firmware = device control | Middleware = connection services.

revision: Software = programs, instructions and related information; a module is a job-doing component, not the smallest unit.
Source code is original; object code comes from a compiler or assembler; machine code is binary run by the processor.
Linker joins object files and libraries; loader puts the program in memory; .exe is a common Windows executable extension.
Program = stored instructions; process = a running instance of a program.
System software manages hardware: OS, device drivers, translators, utilities, firmware. MS-DOS is an OS.
Application software (end-user software) does user tasks; word processors, spreadsheets and media players are applications.
Defragmentation reorganises scattered file fragments on a hard disk; Disk Cleanup deletes unnecessary files; SSDs use TRIM.
ERP = Enterprise Resource Planning; SAP is a company. Finacle (Infosys) is vertical banking software; Bacs is a UK payment system.
Horizontal software serves many industries; vertical software serves one industry or profession.
Open source gives source rights (Linux kernel, Firefox, VLC); closed source is withheld (MS Office, Tally, Avast).
Freeware = no purchase price; shareware = evaluation then payment; trialware = limited trial; nagware = repeated reminders.
EULA = End User License Agreement; public-domain software has no copyright; freeware and open source can still be copyrighted.
Compiler translates source before execution; interpreter executes via a runtime; assembler turns assembly into object code.
Java: compiler gives bytecode, then the JVM interprets it and often uses just-in-time compilation.
Patch = targeted fix; update = fixes or small changes; upgrade = newer, more capable version; bug = defect.
Firmware sits in non-volatile memory (BIOS/UEFI, routers, printers); middleware is the glue connecting applications.
